subject: Re: Context ceiling and latency trade-offs — decision log & next steps
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Nora Patel <nora.patel@veridian.ai>, Tim Liao <tim.liao@veridian.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-04T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo recap: context ceilings, streaming needs, and open questions

Hi Nora / Tim — thanks again for the demo time earlier. Quick recap of what we captured and a few immediate asks so we can size a targeted Dedicated trial: 

1) Workload shape (what you told us):
- Typical request: conversational retrieval augmented generation.
- Median input length: ~2,400 input tokens (retrieved docs + user prompt).
- Expected output: 800–1,500 tokens (multi-turn summaries and instructions).
- Peak simultaneous users during testing window: 120 concurrent active sessions; spikes up to ~220 for 2–3 minutes.

2) Performance/SLO goals you stated:
- Partial streaming latency target (first partial token): p95 <= 120 ms for interactive UI.
- Full response p95: <= 2.0 s for replies under 800 output tokens; allow up to 5 s for ~1,500-token outputs if necessary.
- Throughput target for Dedicated pilot: sustained 60 requests/sec with 10% headroom.

3) Key constraint: combined context ceiling (input + output) should support up to 10k tokens. You mentioned sometimes you want to push to 12k for batch analysis; that would be best-effort and may invoke fallback/denial policies.

Open questions / actions for Veridian: 
- Can you share a 48-hour sample of token-length distribution (input/output) and a sample of 50 representative long requests? We will use it to tune batching & caching.
- Confirm whether occasional 12k-context requests must succeed (and pay more) or can be rejected with a clear client error.

Internal note: CC-ing Soojin to capture the perf/quantization constraints for Dedicated sizing.

Attachments: I attached our quick perf matrix template and the demo snippet you asked for.

Thanks —
Markus Klein

From: Nora Patel <nora.patel@veridian.ai>

Cc: Tim Liao <tim.liao@veridian.ai>
Date: 2027-05-04T17:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: context ceilings, streaming needs, and open questions

Thanks Markus — quick clarifications from our side: 

- Sample data: attaching a high-level token histogram for the past week (see attached). We'll export the 50 examples you asked for by EOD tomorrow.
- On 12k contexts: those are rare (around 0.4% of requests) and we absolutely need them to complete; clients treat them as high-value batch jobs rather than interactive. They can tolerate higher latency (up to ~12–20 s) but must not be silently dropped.
- Streaming: we rely on partial tokens for rendering progressive answers; the UX needs first partial within ~150 ms at p95. If your model routing can't guarantee that for the largest contexts, we prefer a graceful degradation that streams the first 200 tokens quickly (low-latency path) and then emits remainder on the compute-heavy path.

Two more asks for Redwood:
1) Can you propose a fallback policy for >10k requests (either route to a batch tier, throttle, or accept with SLA differentials)?
2) Please confirm whether prefix/KV caching would help given we have heavy document overlap across sessions.

Regards,
Nora Patel
Head of ML Infrastructure | Veridian AI
nora.patel@veridian.ai

Attachment: veridian_token_histogram_20270504.csv

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Nora Patel <nora.patel@veridian.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-04T19:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: context ceilings, streaming needs, and open questions

Nora — thanks for the details. Technical readouts / proposals below. I'm attaching a quick token-latency matrix we populated from a 4k / 8k / 12k synthetic run.

Summary:
- We can meet the interactive streaming first-partial latency (p95 <= 150 ms) for requests where combined context <= 6k tokens on our current dedicated instance shapes (A3 / q8 quantized variants).
- For 6k–10k combined contexts, p95 first-partial tends to drift to 180–350 ms depending on cache hit rates; full completion time depends on output length and model choice (1.2–6 s observed).
- 12k combined contexts are feasible but require either:
  a) a larger instance type (adds ~2.2x cost) and optimistic KV-cache warm state, or
  b) accept a dual-path: fast-path for initial 200 tokens (serve from a smaller context window model + cache) then patch remaining output via a long-job runner.

Recommendations for the pilot:
1) Dedicated baseline: provision capacity for sustained 70 rps with concurrency target 200 (sessions), using a mix of q8 70B models for long contexts and smaller 20–30B for fast-path streaming.
2) Implement an explicit server-side policy: requests with combined context > 10k go to "batch-tier" by default (async job with doc status), but clients can opt-in to a premium synchronous lane — we will enforce a higher per-request cost and relaxed latency SLO.
3) Enable prefix/KV caching; given your doc overlap note, we estimate up to ~35% token saving on average which materially reduces latency for 6k+ contexts.

Action items for us: Soojin -> prototype a dual-path canary and share perf matrix by tomorrow. Markus -> verify commercial acceptance of premium lane with the Veridian procurement team.

-Soojin
Soojin Lee
Principal Perf Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai

Attachment: latency_token_matrix.csv

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Nora Patel <nora.patel@veridian.ai>, Tim Liao <tim.liao@veridian.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-05T09:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Context ceiling and latency trade-offs — decision log & next steps

Nora / Tim — thanks for the quick responses and for sending the histogram. This thread becomes our decision log for the pilot scoping. Key decisions and next steps below: 

Decisions made (pilot scope):
- Pilot SLOs: Partial-stream p95 <= 150 ms for combined context <= 6k; partial-stream p95 <= 350 ms for 6k–10k. Full-response p95 <= 2.5 s for outputs <= 1k tokens; allow up to 12 s for 12k-context premium synchronous jobs.
- Fallback policy: default for combined context > 10k is to move to batch-tier (async job). Customers may opt-in to premium sync lane (higher per-request price, explicit SLA exceptions).
- Caching: enable prefix/KV caching for pilot; target hit-rate improvement 20–40% based on samples.

Concrete next steps: 
1) Veridian to share the 50 long-request samples and a 48-hour token-length distribution export (due: 2027-05-06 EOD) — Nora.
2) Redwood to deliver:
   - Soojin to run canary (dual-path) and share the latency_token_matrix + cost delta by 2027-05-06 17:00 PT.
   - Lauren to produce a preliminary Dedicated sizing and cost estimate (including premium lane pricing) by 2027-05-07.
3) Commercial: Markus to open SOW draft with proposed pilot terms and premium-lane pricing; target sign-off call next week.

If Veridian is aligned, I'll schedule a 30-minute procurement sync (Markus + Lauren + Nora + Tim) for Wed 2027-05-12 to review SOW and SLA annex.

Thanks all — looking forward to the pilot.

-Markus Klein
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai
